one_line_contribution: A pre-registered ALFWorld collision study that crosses a QLoRA dose ladder trained on a post-rule-change procedure with stale, fresh, mixed and decoy retrieved demonstrations, and asks the one thing the compliance-trap literature has not: whether any reachable amount of parametric training helps the agent produce the new step after the environment has already answered 'Nothing happens.' to the stale context item, plus a costed routing plot (rule sentence vs. validity filter vs. retraining).
closest_prior_work: The Compliance Trap, arXiv:2607.10608 (verified via the literature command, s2 channel: E-P-R framework asking where retrieved memory first changes an action, whether it propagates, and whether the agent recovers after leaving the correct path; conflicting memory is adopted early, recovery is weak, stronger agents are hurt more). It remains the nearest work and the proposal positions honestly against it, but the positioning is thinner than the abstract admits: the headline 'context dominance survives environmental feedback' is, for the W_none arm, precisely 2607.10608's weak-recovery result reproduced on a new synthetic shift. The genuinely untested content narrows to one contrast, D_e = AR@6(W_post-e, C_pre) - AR@6(W_none, C_pre), replicated across four rungs. Two further threats. (1) arXiv:2608.15008 'Harness the Memory: A Holistic Evaluation of Memory Substrates in Memory Agents' (verified via hf; title and one-line summary only, no full abstract retrieved) is a controlled harness evaluation covering text records, refinement-based memories and parametric updates across operating regimes, concluding that trade-offs are regime-dependent and that adaptive substrate routing is needed. That is the same routing framing the abstract claims 'no hybrid paper has costed'. It is named in the Stage-1 brief itself, yet appears nowhere in the proposal's Related Work or Preprint Collision Check - the single most conspicuous omission in the submission, and one an AC will notice because the brief handed it over. I could not confirm whether it runs a weights-vs-context conflict cell, so it is a positioning threat rather than a collision. (2) arXiv:2305.13300 (Adaptive Chameleon or Stubborn Sloth, ICLR, 385 citations, verified via s2/hf) plus arXiv:2506.06485, arXiv:2503.15888 (CK-PLUG) and arXiv:2407.13048 (all verified) already establish the direction on single answers; the proposal concedes this and demotes the entry-point contrast to a manipulation check, which is the right call but leaves less new territory than the title implies.
strongest_objection: The result is largely determined by the intensity mismatch built into the two channels, and the two headline claims are therefore not fair substrate comparisons. On the context side the intervention is a full same-task expert demonstration whose action sequence is exactly the wrong procedure, dropped into a ReAct prompt that treats demonstrations as templates. On the weights side it is QLoRA rank 32-128 for 2-8 epochs over ~800 walkthroughs. That a same-task demonstration beats 1.1-5.5 GPU-hours of adapter training is close to a foregone conclusion, and 'no reachable dose protects' is a statement about this node's budget rather than about substrates - the proposal says so in Risk Factors, which is honest but also concedes the general claim away. The asymmetry prediction P2b is worse: W_pre is trained on pre-rule walkthroughs, which contain no 'activate' step, on a base model that already never issues 'activate'. W_pre therefore encodes essentially nothing that conflicts with the new rule beyond what W_none already encodes, so 'stale weights do not trap the agent' (AR@6(W_pre, C_none) >= AR@6(W_none, C_none) - 10) is close to guaranteed by construction - the same near-definitional defect that sank opposite_sided_failure_under_shift in round 2, relocated from an append-only bank to an inert LoRA. Second, the statistics are asymmetric in favour of the hypothesis. Confirmation of P1 needs only a point estimate <= 10 with a CI excluding 25, while falsification needs D_e >= 25 with a CI excluding 10; with a stated MDE of +/-9 to +/-10 on AR@6, a real protective effect of 12-18 points - over half of E0 - passes the confirmation criterion and fails the falsification criterion. The equivalence margin (10) and the noise floor (9) are the same size, so the headline is a low-powered non-rejection presented as a claim, which is what the brief's power rule was written to prevent. Third, the practical payload is thinner than sold: if C_mix+filter works (P5) that transposes MemStrata's verified result (arXiv:2606.26511, RAG serves superseded values 15-40% of the time, validity filtering drives it to ~0%) into an agent setting, and if R works (P4) the finding is that telling the model the new rule works.
what_would_fix_it: Three changes, in order of how much they buy. (1) Make the asymmetry a substrate test by intensity-matching the two stale channels: add a weights arm trained on an actively conflicting post-rule procedure (e.g. walkthroughs that activate the wrong receptacle, or that keep the pre-rule sequence at the same dose as the winning post-rule rung), then pre-register the matching condition on the entry-point manipulation check - only compare recovery between channels whose pre-feedback wrong-action rates are within, say, 10 points. Without that, P2b compares an inert adapter to a same-task demonstration and reports the difference as a property of substrates. (2) Add the one parametric intervention that prior work says makes weights win: CK-PLUG (arXiv:2503.15888, ~0 GPU-h, sits on the Pareto plot next to R and the filter) and/or a small knowledge-preference-tuned arm in the style of arXiv:2407.13048, which the proposal explicitly excludes and then relies on excluding. As written, 'no reachable dose protects' is asserted while deliberately omitting the dose type designed to protect. (3) Fix the asymmetric inference: make P1 a two-sided pre-registered equivalence test at a margin the design can actually resolve (margin >= 2x the MDE, i.e. more seeds or a wider ID pool if the margin stays at 10), and report any D_e between the MDE and the margin as unresolved rather than as confirmation. Also cite and differentiate arXiv:2608.15008 explicitly - the routing-question framing in the abstract cannot stand while the substrate benchmark named in the brief goes unaddressed.
missing_baseline: A stale-weights arm that actually encodes a conflicting procedure, matched in entry-point wrongness to C_pre (call it W_wrong: post-rule targets with the wrong activation, or pre-rule targets trained to the same dose as the strongest post-rule rung). W_pre as specified is trained on a procedure the base model already follows, so it cannot distinguish 'stale weights are harmless' from 'this LoRA changed nothing', and the hypothesis's asymmetry claim goes untested. Second omission, directly relevant to the headline: an inference-time or preference-trained parametric-reliance arm - CK-PLUG (arXiv:2503.15888) at ~0 GPU-h, or a knowledge-preference-tuned student (arXiv:2407.13048) - since the Pareto plot's conclusion ('the lever is retrieval, not retraining') is drawn with the one published lever that makes weights win left off the plot by design.

Also confirmed as existing by appearing in my searches: 2506.06485, 2503.15888, 2606.17591, 2605.29463, 2607.28272, 2601.11653, 2604.27003, 2608.12218. Could NOT verify this session: 2605.09315, 2605.12978, 2602.16066, 2405.05904, 2503.05919 - of these only 2405.05904 (Gekhman, fine-tuning learns new facts slowly) is load-bearing, for the over-training caveat, and I know it from memory but label it unverified here. Judgement of the check itself: it is one of the better ones I have seen from this pipeline - five queries with IDs, explicit individual resolutions, explicit statement of which round-1 citations were dropped as no longer load-bearing, and an honest 'no collision' rather than an assertion of novelty from silence. But it has one hole that matters, and the brief handed it over: 2608.15008, the substrate benchmark whose stated conclusion is 'no substrate dominates, routing is necessary', is searched neither in round 1 nor round 2 and is cited nowhere in the proposal, while the abstract claims to decide 'a routing question no hybrid paper has costed'. 2608.12218 and 2604.27251, both directly adjacent to the dose-ladder premise and to P4, are likewise absent. The check establishes that nobody has run this exact collision; it does not establish that the routing framing is unoccupied.
